title: Snow, flat tires and failed dates through Nashville and Georgetown
summary: Bad weather cancels the Nashville dance and a flat tire makes them miss Georgetown, leaving Charles to give up his suitcase to pay a lodging bill.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We stayed around Memphis a few weeks. And we got ourselves together on our way back to Cincinnati, Ohio. We get in the two cars and left Memphis on our way to Nashville, Tennessee to play a dance. We ran into a big snow, we get to Nashville, the dance was called off, on account of bad weather. So we left there, our next booking was in Georgetown, Kentucky. Now this job was going to pay us $125.00, which was a lot of money back in 1933.

We had a flat tire going to Georgetown, up in Kentucky and it was so cold till we took one of the spare tires and made a fire to keep from freezing, and we finally took the other spare and put it on the back wheel. Each man in the band, picked the rear of that car up to put that spare tire on. We made it to Lexington, Kentucky. And to Georgetown, we got

there too late to play that dance. So we were losers all the way around. We made it back to Lexington, we were booked there for a dance, didn't make enough money to pay for our lodging. My brother had to leave his suitcase and all of his clothes to bail us out.
